created by geminiI had one API. It had three endpoints, an API key header, and pagination on the list endpoint. Nothing fancy, but not a toy either.
Here’s friends link https://medium.com/@inprogrammer/i-built-an-mcp-server-in-30-minutes-claude-and-cursor-could-use-my-api-immediately-f0592dcec24e?sk=bc15c23902acb6a3b080769b85c3449b
Then I spent four separate weekends writing custom integrations so Claude Desktop, then Cursor, then a random internal chatbot, could each “talk” to that same API. Every weekend looked the same. I wrote a new adapter for auth. I wrote a new adapter for turning errors into something the model could read. I wrote a new adapter for looping through paginated results. Three clients, three copies of the same logic, three separate places for bugs to hide.
That is the moment I got mad enough to try MCP.
Thirty minutes later I had a working server. Claude Desktop and Cursor could both call my API without me writing a single custom adapter for either one. Here is exactly what disappeared once the server was up:

• No more per client auth code. One API key, read once, from an environment variable.

• No more per client error handling. One raise_for_status() call, and the protocol…
